findings.reason: §18 must name `reckon/_schema.py:plan_executable_remainder` as the owner and decide whether the count reader shares the landing-subtraction rule or keeps its own with a stated reason, and must correct the consumer claim, or the de-duplication it performs is incomplete and two surfaces answer the same question differently.
findings.text: §18 states "only two readers answer 'which sections are still work'" (`promotion._plan_remaining_sections`, `doccheck._implementable_section_ids`) and that `roadmap.implementable_sections` "is what the roadmap, the MCP views and the run store consume"; but a third declaration-map state reader exists, `reckon/_schema.py:plan_executable_remainder`, returning a count (`int | None`) whose docstring fixes the opposite landing rule — "Landing evidence records a node outcome; it does not close the section. Only an explicit `done` reclassification removes declared work" — and its value is what the crew closure drain reads at `reckon/crew/runs.py:1486` (via `metadata_index._plan_record`/`plan_derivations`, not the roadmap reader), so the run-store half of §18's claim names the wrong producer; extending `roadmap.implementable_sections` with landing subtraction while `plan_executable_remainder` keeps "landings do not close a section" makes the gate's outstanding set and the drain's declared remainder diverge in exactly the landed-but-not-done case §18 exists to resolve

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the per-section digesting, the identity derivation and the coverage join are hidden behind `plan_fingerprint`, one hoisted `section_record_id` and one private predicate; §17 consolidates nine walked sites onto one private parser exposed by a single public reader, so surface shrinks while behaviour grows, which is the shape the item asks for.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §18 enumerates only two readers of the declaration map's "still work" question and leaves a third standing, `_schema.plan_executable_remainder`, whose landing rule is the opposite of the one §18 is about to add.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; the only family any of the three sections grows is public_definitions, and §16/§17/§18 name the single added name (`plan_headings`), the move of `landed_section_ids` (net zero), the private retirements, and the net of one across the three, with §18 adding none; no section adds a CLI option, MCP view or refusal family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — each section cites and extends the mechanism it most resembles: §17 reuses `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`/`structured_section_spans` rather than adding a scanner, §18 extends the existing `roadmap.implementable_sections` rather than minting a reader, §16 extends the existing `plan_fingerprint`/`_fingerprint_forms` pair; I opened each and each exists as described.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the two public readers over the parser are justified in §17 (spans-only for the store's boundary protection versus identity derivation for the heading walks), and §16's coverage predicate is a genuine two-reader join that says why `read_plan_review`'s one-record join cannot be extended to a set question.
